rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE ENTRY OF FOREIGN TOBACCO, CIGAR AND CIGARETTE MANUFACTURERS, DISTRIBUTORS, DEALERS AND/OR EXPORTERS INTO THE PHILIPPINES AND PHASING OUT OF THE EXISTING DOMESTIC TOBACCO INDUSTRY WITHIN A PERIOD OF TEN (10) YEARS, PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS HEREOF AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Tobacco Abolition Law of 1999".  The local toabacco industry shall be phased out within a period of ten (10) years from effectivity of this Act after which any activity involving the plantation and/or cultivation of tobacco and the production, manufacture, distribution and/or sale of any and all tobacco products shall be prohibited within the Philippine territory. During this period, the National Toabacco Adminsitration (NTA), in coordination with other government agencies formulate and establish programs and projects that will assist the persons engaged in and involved with the tobacco industry to have other livelihood opportunities and sources of income.
rows.status: Substituted by HB12771

rows.abstract: "Chambers of Commerce and Industry Act of 1999". Rationale: The bill seeks to promote the growth of chambers of commerce and industry (CCIs) nationwide. Presently, there is not chamber of commerce and industry system for all business and economic sectors. Chambers have thus uncontrollably mushroomed across the country with overlapping and duplication of functions and services resulting in inefficiency, and inability6 to provide value added services for its members, among others. For purposes ofenhancing the support of functions of CCI's in national economic growth, there is felt a need to establish a set of standards for greater efficiencies and effectiveness of Philippine CCI's.

rows.abstract: The bill proposes to limit the hours of operation of nightclubs, cocktail lounges, bars and similar establishments serving liquor, wine or intoxicating drinks from 5:00 p.m. to 1:00 a.m.  It also prohibits patrons of such establishments from carrying firearms insie, consequently, depositing the same with the management or opertor, and enjoins the owner, oeprators or manager not to allow persons with criminal record or of questionable character from entering such establishments. rows.abstract: In 1995, the Death Penalty Law was reinstated. Included in this Law was the imposition of death penalty on carnapping if it included murder and rape. However, despite the inclusion of carnapping as one of those liable with death penalty, there has been an increase in the incidence of carnapping. Carnappers today are even more sly. They use "high technology" gadgets in thier operations. Thus, there is a need to impose stricter penalties on carnapping.

rows.abstract: Rationale: This bill seeks to provide our poor people especially those from the province the equal opportunity to fight and look for justice in a legal battle in courts and other judicial bodies in Manila. rows.title_full: AN ACT RESTORING THE TAX EXEMPTION PRIVILEGES OF LOCAL WATER DISTRICTS UNDER SECTION 46 OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 198, AS AMENDED AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Section 46 of Presidential Decree Number 198, as amended, granting TAX EXEMPTION PRIVILEGES to local water districts is hereby RESTORED and shall be effective for a period of ten (10) years from approval of this Act. Water districts shall likewise be exempted from the provision of Republic Act Number 7656 requiring government-owne d and controlled corporations (GOCCs) to remit fifty percent (50%) of their annual net income to the National Government, provided that, the amount supposed to be remitted is utilized by the water district concerned for the continuing and improvement of its system.

rows.author: C093
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTING POLICIES GOVERNING THE HOUSEHOLD EMPLOYMENT INDUSTRY, ESTABLISHING A STANDARD OF PROTECTION AND PROMOTING THE WELFARE OF HOUSEHOLD HELPERS AND THEIR FAMILIES
rows.abstract: "BATAS KASAMBAHAY" Rationale: The proposed Batas Kasambahay seeks to redress the grave injustice on this significant section of the labor force, by providing the basic structure that would uphold their dignity and protect their rights and privileges. Let it not be construed however, that the Batas Kasambahay will fully correct the societal imbalance prevalent in this sector, for the circumstances are so complex and the inter-relations hips so intricate. But we have to start somewhere. Let the Batas Kasambahay be the springboard by which other laws that seek to protect the interests of our fellow Filipinos are enacted by this august body.
